texts.preamble: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Varun Vashishta on 25 November, 2016 In The Court Of Sh. Ashu Garg, Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 39/08 Unique Case Id No. 02403R0278342008 (new no.41371/2016) Date of Institution: 07.04.2008 Date of reserving judgement: 16.11.2016 Date of pronouncement: 25.11.2016 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus Varun Vashishta S/o. Sh.Kamal Vashishta R/o. Gg-Ii, 76B, Vikas Puri, New Delhi-110018. ... Accused Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused Varun Vashishta is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Bengali Sweets & Restaurants, from where the food article, that is, 'Besan Ke Laddu' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 06.11.2007, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) V.P.S.Chaudhary and Field Assistant (FA) Balwant Shah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Pramod Kumar reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. Bengali Sweets & Restaurants at Shop No. 5, F Block, DDA Market, Vikas Puri, New Delhi-110018, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored for sale for human consumption. The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Besan Ke Laddu from the vendor lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed. The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Varun Vashishta on 25 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145352032/ 1 PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 07.12.2007, the PA found the sample to be not conforming to the standards of Vanaspati declared as an ingredient on the ground that it gave negative Baudouin Test. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.04.2008 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 07.04.2008. The accused appeared but never filed application under section 13(2) of PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample to be analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). 4. Based on the report of the PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against the accused on 03.02.2009 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act, being violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. At the trial, prosecution initially examined four witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 Sh. Pramod Kumar, PW-3 FA Balwant Shah and PW-4 FI V.P.S.Chaudhary were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 06.11.2007 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms Besan Ke Laddu lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration, breaking it into smallest possible pieces, mixing/ homogenizing it, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, adding 40 drops of formalin in each bottle as preservative, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, Report under Rule 9(e) Ex. PW-1/D, PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/F and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/E. PA report Ex. PW-1/G was received and investigation was started. Letter Ex. PW-1/G was written to the STO and its reply sought. After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/H was taken from the Director PFA and the complaint Ex. PW- 1/I was filed in the court. A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex. PW-1/J was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex. PW-1/K through PW-2 FI S.B.Sharma. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the sampling method was not proper or that the accused had been falsely implicated. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was initially recorded on 02.11.2010 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Though he admitted the proceedings dated 06.11.2007, yet he questioned the PA report on the ground that the BT Test gives negative result when the Vanaspati is heated. Delhi Administration / Food Inspector vs Varun Vashishta on 25 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145352032/ 2 7. After hearing the matter, vide order dated 07.10.2016, this court was of the view that the evidence of Public Analyst who had analyzed the sample and gave report was necessary. As such, the said Public Analyst was summoned as a witness. 8. PA Smt. Mohini Shrivastava who had given report Ex. PW-1/G was examined as PW-5 to clarify the position. She deposed that the BT Test was conducted to determine the presence of sesame oil (til oil) in Vanaspati which is mandatory to be added as per PFA Rules. During cross-examination, she accepted that no standards have been prescribed for Besan Ke Laddu and the sample was considered as a proprietary food. She accepted that upon heating at high temperature of Vanaspati or any food article prepared from Vanaspati, the sesamol content gets degraded due to which BT Test might give negative result. She also admitted that this view has been documented in the book by David Pearson which is a standard recognized literature in the field.
texts.arguments: 9. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings of the PA report dated 07.12.2007. It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony. 10. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the sample proceedings were not conducted properly and that there are various missing links in the testimony of witnesses. Ld. Counsel has strongly contended that there is no standard for Besan Ke Laddu and the standards of Vanaspati cannot be applied to such a product particularly when the PA herself has admitted that BT Test might give negative result upon heating.

It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony.
